Manger used his OMEC connections to help Gasom, a company that contracted him, to attract top engineering talent.\n\nAfter helping his home region find foreign direct investment, he diversified his investments. Gus saw great potential in Anrica, as a middle-ground between the most prominent cities. He made significant investments there in the early 1940s, founding and running a successful logistics and tourism company. His strong relations with the city led him to acquire minority ownership in FC Anrica, the city's football club.\n\nIn 1943 he was appointed deputy to the Minister of Economy, Commerce, and Energy of Tarquin Soll's 4th cabinet. After the party congress of 1946 and the loss of party leadership of Tarquin Soll, Gus joined the Alphonso government as Minister of Development. Gus was particularly successful in helping rural poverty reduction through international investment attraction, arranging high-value export routes for locally produced agricultural goods, and adjusting import and export taxes to drive the generated economic value up in Sordland. \n\nBetween 1950 and 1952, he was crucial in arranging landmark trade deals with countries like Rizia, Lespia, and Anraka to improve the trade deficit of Sordland and help the economy to stabilize. Manger worked tirelessly during and after the 51 recession with the \"Three Econs,\" consisting of Edith Agnoc, Mikail Aven, and Symon Holl, and helped Sordland avoid economic depression.\n\nHe eventually supported Anton Rayne in 1953 after the collapse of the Alphonso cabinet. He also served as president of the University of Valgen and Gelsord School of Medicine.\n\nBefore his political career, Paskal wrote 8 books, one of which was a best-seller called ‘’The Unfortunate Man,’’ where he tells the story of a family of poverty-stricken miners. He became known as a writer who depicts the struggles of Sordish life from a realistic frame, which brought him praise from the middle class and the civil rights groups.\n\nHe was elected to the assembly in 1945 and advocated for new workplace safety regulations and a workers compensation program. He was an important force in the shaping of the nation’s first social security policies. Initially a supporter of Ewald Alphonso’s programs, Paskal eventually turned against the free market reforms and the president’s management of them, stating that it drained badly needed resources away from welfare programs. He gave his support to Anton Rayne in 1953, and was appointed as a minister after the elections.\n\nIn 1957, Paskal resigned from his position as minister due to disagreements with President Rayne.",

He is regarded by some Sollists as the founder of the Republic of Sordland since the first years of the republic between 1923 and 1927 were short lived due to the Civil War. Soll assumed the post in 1929 by ending the Sordish Civil War and taking control of the government under military rule. He is the founder of the United Sordland Party. He is regarded as the most significant and controversial person in Sordland’s history.\n\nTarquin was a colonel and the commander of the 6th army of the Sordish Armed Forces when General Luderin executed a military coup in 1927, which he did not join. Later in 1927, Civil War broke out between armies of the Sordish military as well as militant political organizations. Following this, Tarquin Soll and the 6th Army joined the war and managed to win several major battles against both General Luderin and General Rikard. In January 1929, the 6th army took control of Holsord and started pushing the rebels to the east. Later in the year, Tarquin Soll put an end to the Sordish Civil War, took control of the government, wrote a new Constitution, and called the Grand National Assembly back to work. He formed the USP and went to elections with one party and became the President of Sordland.\n\nHis first years saw many developments in Sordland, restoring and surpassing the pre-Civil War production levels. He invested heavily into infrastructure, healthcare and police forces. Many forgotten areas of Sordland were provided with services for the first time in their history during Soll administration. He also addressed the much problematic energy problem of Sordland with the Soll Dam project in Erzaren which triggered the 1933 Izzam Incident and a long conflict with Bludish separatists.\n\nAfter his first term as President, Tarquin called for elections in 1933 and ran as a candidate in the first ever elections of Sordland with multiple parties, which still resulted in a massive win for Tarquin Soll and the USP. In total he won five elections and served as President of Sordland for twenty years.\n\nHis later terms saw further economic developments along with an increase in political and racial tensions in Sordland. Many Bludish activists and politicians were arrested, communists were detained for suspected crimes against the state. The media was under his control and censored the opposing voices. Many different political parties entered politics to oppose Tarquin Soll’s leadership, and several of them were closed down.\n\nIn the 1940’s, the opposition against Tarquin Soll reached new heights, triggering major protests against him within the USP. In the late 1940’s, the new reformist wing in the party saw a great increase in its influence and started to challenge Tarquin. He went on to serve as President of Sordland until 1949.\n\nAfter his resignation as president, he moved to reside in Duru Island at the mouth of the Gulf of Nargis. He invited the famous poet Bernard Circas to join the party ahead of their first elections in 1953, but was rejected.\n\nIn the ‘53 elections, he got just below 8% of the general vote, failing to pass the election threshold. Later, Bron transitioned to politics, joining the United Sordland Party (USP.) In 1932, he took on the role as Mayor of Deyr.\n\nInitially a moderate on racial issues, Bron adopted a hard-line nationalist stance after the Izzam Incident and the subsequent revolt in Bergia by the Bludish Freedom Front. Bron earned national notoriety when he stood in front of the entrance of the Archsantuary of Deyr with armed policemen, blocking the path of Bludish Nurists and not allowing them to attend the Descension Day rituals in 1934.\n\nAfter the formation of the Special Zone in Bergia in 1935, he was appointed as the head of the Counter-Separatism Unit in the Ministry of the Interior. When Dewlen Arge declared a rebellion in Bergia in 1935, he worked extensively with the governor on the fight against the BFF. \n\nIn 1941, he was appointed as the Governor of the Special Zone of Bergia by President Tarquin Soll. During his tenure as governor, he promoted industrial development, increased taxes and improved regional law enforcement. He is also credited for the arrest of the BFF leader, Dewlen Arge, due to his massive budget increases of the regional police forces, and leading the operation of his capture. He was later appointed as governor again in 1947 and later in 1953 by President Ewald Alphonso, retaining his position as governor.\n\nIn 1957, he was kidnapped by Bludish Freedom Front militants and was taken hostage in Soll Dam. Together, they also stopped the invading armies and regained some of the lost territories. Meanwhile, Valgos stopped their raids into Agnolia, but the Rumburg war exhaustion was proving too damaging for the little gains made. In 1710, a peace treaty was signed between the three nations.\n\nWhen Lenna passed away in 1740, the two unified countries split again and Agnolia fell into a civil war between three families claiming the kingdom. The duke of West Agnolia decided to remain in Renan and did not join the conflict. The territory was later renamed Agnland. After the civil war, Agnolia was re-established as a merchant republic with a Rector at its head.\n\nIn the early 19th century, the world witnessed the beginning of the Century of Revolutions. The government introduced a multi-party system and scheduled the first elections to be held in 1927.\n\nFollowing the multi-party reforms, many political parties were formed, some of which promoted monarchism, anti-secularism and anti-communism. He ordered the arrest of President Wisci and the executions of hundreds of revolutionaries and communist politicians, effectively ending the era of ‘the First Republic of Sordland’.\n\nIn 1928, following the mass executions of the martial law period, General Rikard attempted to seize power from Luderin and led an attack against the new administration. This led to the start of the Sordish Civil War, which lasted until 1929.\n\nIn 1929, the Sordish Civil War was brought to an end by Colonel Tarquin Soll and his 6th Army, which successfully destroyed both General Rikard and Luderin’s forces. He captured Holsord and became the de-facto head of the state.\n\nDuring his de-facto rule, Soll wrote a new constitution and formed the United Sordland Party. In the late 1930s, he oversaw major urban development projects, including the landmark Alvarez Towers and the Falenco Five, a large-scale residential complex consisting of 5,000 apartment units in the city of Falenco.\n\nIn 1940, Patricio Alvarez was investigated by the Lespian Anti-Corruption Force for profiteering, but the case was dropped that same year following his entry into politics as a member of the Democrazia Lespia party. He would later admit that part of his decision to pursue public office was to shield himself from legal prosecution.\n\nOver the course of the early to mid-1940s, Alvarez emerged as a prominent voice within the party, working closely with his political mentor, Serdin Alvarro, the former party leader. Though still in opposition to the ruling Partido Libertà Nazionale, their proposals gained traction in business circles and media hubs, particularly in Ventrie City, amid growing anxieties over global capital instability.\n\nBy the late 1940s, Alvarez had consolidated control over Democrazia Lespia and launched a sweeping national campaign ahead of the 1948 elections, leveraging his expansive business ties and media network. His victory in 1949 led to the establishment of the Lespian Capital Protection Agency, enacted in cooperation with the influential Magical Eight corporate bloc. Although Prime Minister Cauren Fidalco and the Partido Libertà Nazionale publicly condemned the direction of Alvarez's reforms, they were ultimately unable to halt the transformation of Lespia’s economic model.\n\nAs Prime Minister, Alvarez implemented sweeping tax reductions, scaled back state regulations, and introduced targeted protectionist measures to preserve national wealth and production. These policies favored megacorporations aligned with his government, granting them regulatory advantages and market access. Miraclists support democracy as the ideal political system to nurture this collective spirit, enabling what they term \"The Human Miracle.\" \n\nThis philosophy holds that tradition and religious beliefs are crucial to maintaining the cultural systems that support human civilizations, advocating a contemplative approach that prioritizes continuity and the collective wisdom of past generations over the transformative promises of radical ideologies.",

This political and economic model diverges from traditional socialism by advocating for a decentralized structure based on labor union federations and people's assemblies, rather than relying on a vanguard party of the proletariat to lead the revolution.\n\nOne of the key principles of Valgslandian Socialism is its opposition to the centralization of power and authority in the hands of a single party. Instead, it promotes the establishment of labor union federations, which are seen as vital instruments for representing the interests of the working class and providing a platform for workers to participate in decision-making processes. This approach aims to empower workers and ensure that the socialist revolution is driven by the collective will of the people, rather than imposed from above by a centralized authority.\n\nAnother crucial aspect of Valgslandian Socialism is its tenet of replacing the state with a federal, economic organization of society. This vision seeks to create a more egalitarian and participatory system, where decisions are made collectively through democratic processes, including people's assemblies and labor unions. In this model, regional and local governments would enjoy greater autonomy, with decision-making power devolved to the grassroots level.\n\nHegel's theory emphasizes the importance of transitioning from a statist form of socialism to a decentralized structure in order to achieve the goals of the socialist revolution. In his view, retaining centralized control over the economy within the state apparatus would ultimately stifle innovation, hinder economic growth, and perpetuate inequality. By contrast, a decentralized system based on a federal democracy would promote cooperation, shared decision-making, and a more equitable distribution of resources.",

By the late 19th century, Arcasia had emerged as a global power, anchoring its influence in the spread of capitalism, liberal democracy, and military dominance. \n\nArcasia secured the world’s largest economy by nominal GDP in the early 20th century. Its corporate sector expanded across continents, universities grew into elite academic institutions, and political freedoms remained broadly protected. At the same time, structural inequalities persisted, particularly between urban financial centers and underdeveloped regions, and its global conduct has come under scrutiny for reported abuses abroad. \n\nSince 1947, Arcasia has been led by President Dwight Walker and the New Democratic Concord. Key industries such as telecommunications, education, transportation, healthcare, and military contracting underwent sweeping deregulation and privatization. Private defense firms like Cerberus International and Palantor Security Solutions rose to prominence during this era.
